correctness.rationale: The first exact local solve gives \(x_k^1=R_\alpha x^0+S_\alpha b_k\). From round two onward, the stored gradient equals the true local gradient, yielding \(x_k^t=S_\alpha x_k^{t-1}+R_\alpha x^{t-1}\). The full-participation server identity and \(h^t=H(\gamma^t-x_\star)\) then give the exact powers \(R_\alpha^t\) and \(S_\alpha^t\). Spectral monotonicity over \([\mu,L]\) proves the two sharp factors, and equalizing them uniquely gives \(\alpha=\sqrt{\mu L}\).

value.rationale: The regularization parameter is the defining tuning control of exact-minimization FedDyn, and the source explicitly says it balances problem-dependent quantities. The common-Hessian family isolates statistical heterogeneity while retaining nontrivial conditioning, and the exact decomposition shows the concrete tradeoff: increasing regularization slows global-average motion but accelerates client consensus. The geometric mean of endpoint curvatures is the unique balance, with a square-root-condition-number factor, and the isotropic case exhibits an exact one-round server solution. These are structurally interpretable tuning facts rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
